coverage.assessment: The telegram, note and timetable chain is intact. The inference that she was carried off by car is cut, so the car-tracking appears unmotivated (F5). The weakened whole-house dust evidence thins the contrast with the brooch at the gate (F1).

Exits and entrances (Julius going upstairs and returning with the letter) are clear. Room 891, King's Cross and the 12.50 are consistent. Small transitions are abrupt but readable: the walk from the station is omitted, and 'Emboldened' now follows only Tommy's wheel-round.

Speakers stay clear. The unattributed 'Is Tuppence found?' after 'Julius was on the platform' still reads as Tommy's line. Henry's turn-taking, the proposal exchange and Julius's interrupted '----' survive.
The porter's uncertainty ('Several people had arrived... could not call to mind') is collapsed into a flat head-shake (F2). The brooch is still limited to 'came as far as here'.
Nothing signals that the boy was right or that the telegram was altered. Sir James stays a 'human oyster' with motives ambiguous. Julius gets no suspicion beyond his brief pocketing of the note.

V3 and the free indirect jealousy-to-elation swing survive. Lost: Tommy's comic modesty and self-deprecation at the reunion (F6), the narrator's hustle-versus-thinking contrast (F3), Tommy's depression on arrival (F4), and the narrator's ending foreshadowing along with some Julius idiom (F7).

The planted contrast between an untouched house and a brooch at the gate is thinned (F1). Tommy as slow worrier versus Julius as hustler is less staged, though the hostage reasoning still shows Tommy thinking.
All six dependencies are intact at both endpoints. The 023 partner trims 'took it for granted he had made a mistake', but the Charing Cross clue still pays off.

dependencies.assessment: The boy's 'Charing Cross' and Tommy's 'Boy must have made a mistake' are both verbatim, and nothing hints the boy was right. The 023 partner keeps the page-boy statement as the overlooked clue, though it trims the 'took it for granted' echo.

evidence.quote: The taxi, sir. I heard her tell the driver Charing Cross and to look sharp.
(Boy must have made a mistake. It was King's Cross, not _Charing_ Cross.)
The page-boy's statement that Miss Cowley drove to Charing Cross.

dependencies.assessment: The locked-room puzzle stays open with no suspicion assigned. The 026 partner keeps the brandy logic.

findings.claim: The revision cuts the house-wide survey ('Everywhere the same tale') and the next-day conclusion that the house had not been entered for a long time. Julius's 'never in this house' now rests only on the dust at the door, and the brooch scene begins with no second search.
findings.counterevidence: Julius's 'Not a sign of a footmark' and Mrs. Sweeny's 'No one's been over the place for a long time' remain.

evidence.quote: They wandered round the deserted house. Everywhere the same tale. Thick layers of dust apparently undisturbed.
were reluctantly forced to the conclusion that the house had not been invaded for some considerable time
On the morrow they were reluctantly forced to the conclusion that the house had not been invaded for some considerable time.
On the morrow, as they were retracing their steps to the gate, Tommy gave a sudden cry

findings.minimal_repair: Restore 'Everywhere the same tale. Thick layers of dust apparently undisturbed.' and the first-draft clause about being forced to that conclusion on the morrow.
findings.plan_relation: Required: 'There is undisturbed dust, then Tuppence's brooch'.
findings.reader_effect: The clue that the whole house is undisturbed while the brooch lies at the gate loses force. The later recognition that the trail was staged has less to rest on.
findings.title: Moat House 'untouched everywhere' evidence reduced to the front-door check

findings.claim: The source separates two things: the porter cannot recall any particular young lady among several arrivals, but he is certain no one asked the way. The revision keeps only the head-shake followed by 'But he was quite certain'. That reads as if he denies she came at all and leaves the 'But' with nothing to contrast against.
findings.counterevidence: The essential point (no enquiry about the way) survives.

evidence.quote: Several people had arrived by the train in question. He could not call to mind one young lady in particular. But he was quite certain
The porter shook his head. Several people had arrived by the train in question.
The porter shook his head. But he was quite certain that no one had asked him the way to the Moat House.

findings.minimal_repair: Restore 'Several people had arrived by the train in question.' before 'But'.
findings.plan_relation: Required item 'porter remembers no enquiry'. The qualification was kept in the first draft.
findings.reader_effect: The testimony now sounds more categorical than the source allows. The precise ambiguity (she may or may not have arrived, but she did not ask the way) is lost.
findings.title: Porter's qualified testimony flattened

findings.claim: The revision removes the narrator's line about Julius's infectious energy and Tommy's tendency to sit and think for half an hour. The first draft had kept it.
findings.counterevidence: 'Tommy nodded abstractedly. He was thinking.' partly preserves the contrast.

evidence.quote: Left to himself, Tommy would probably have sat down to think things out for a good half-hour before he decided on a plan of action.
The energy of Julius was infectious. Left to himself, Tommy would probably have sat down to think things out for a good half-hour.

findings.minimal_repair: Reinstate the first-draft paragraph 94 sentence before the Bradshaw handover.
findings.plan_relation: The voice profile calls for narrative generalisation about types. This was not an authorised cut.
findings.reader_effect: This loses a characteristic type-generalisation and the contrast that frames Tommy's pause to reason about the hostage. That slow, worrying habit of mind is the one later praised and analysed.
findings.title: Narrator's Julius-hustle versus Tommy-thinking contrast cut

findings.claim: The leaden-weight depression and 'three hours was more than enough for Mr. Brown' are both gone. The scene jumps from the porter to the boy at seven o'clock.
findings.counterevidence: The desolate gate and house description carries some of the mood.

findings.claim: The source and the first draft explain the shift of tactics: she must have been carried away in a car. The revision goes straight to tracking every car with no stated reason.

findings.title: Car-abduction inference cut before the car hunt

findings.claim: The first draft cut 'I'm a bit of an ass'. The revision further cuts 'One or two,' replied Tommy modestly, 'order now. It's going to be a long story', 'Bit of a slip on my part', and Julius's British-calm jibe.
findings.counterevidence: 'I was in such a funk I had to think of something' survives as the key admission.

Bit of a slip on my part, that! But it wasn’t the sort of thing a fellow would be likely to guess.

Tommy plunged into his recital.

findings.claim: The revision drops 'But the course of events was not to follow the plan Julius had laid down' and 'Sleuths! It was a piece of damn-fool foolishness!'. The first draft had kept both.
findings.counterevidence: The V8 hook and 'I thought that lawyer chap had quit!' remain.

But the course of events was not to follow the plan Julius had laid down.

findings.minimal_repair: Restore the narrator sentence before 'Later in the day'.

findings.reader_effect: This reduces the narrator's presence before the hook and Julius's distinctive idiom.
findings.title: Narrator's ending foreshadowing and Julius's self-mockery cut

strengths: Restores Julius's first 'We ought to gee along together very well', so his later 'Yes, we ought to gee along...' is a true echo again.
Drops the first draft's dangling 'that pub' after the Yorkshire Arms had been cut.
Keeps the proposal sequence (pocketing, 'butt in', the broken-off 'looking out for----', V3 resentment, 'Refuses?', the note, 'Darling Tuppence') with its emotional swing intact.
Preserves the hostage logic, 'I've great faith in Tuppence', the 23rd and 29th dating, and the Peel Edgerton hook with Julius's closing 'Queer'.
summary: The revision keeps all eight verbatim anchors, the clue chain (Charing Cross and its dismissal, the telegram text, the 'TUPPENCE' signature, the note being handed over, 'hasn't got wings', the hostage logic) and every planned dependency. It also fixes two first-draft residues: the orphaned 'Yes, we ought to gee along' echo and the dangling 'that pub'. Its own extra cuts weaken the Moat House evidence (the dust is checked only at the door, and the next-day conclusion is gone), flatten the porter's qualified testimony, and strip several Tommy/Julius temperament cues and narrator beats. None of this is a blocker.
